text:
maria: heads up — after the kv-cache packing change i pushed yesterday, i'm seeing 95p token latency go up for short-response flows when prefix-hit ratio > 70% :thinking:
kevin: ugh. which part regressed? batching, kernel selection, or memcpy spikes?
sasha: my traces show a lot of tiny batches (batch size 1-3) that are dominated by kernel-switch overhead. also garbage KV cache alignment causing extra copy.
maria: exact. timeline: cache hits improved token count but we ended up with many mixed batches (hit + miss) so the batcher chooses conservative token_budget and ends up forming many small windows.
kevin: could be the batch formation policy that greedily flushes when token budget threshold reached. maybe add smoothing: maintain EWMA target tokens per batch and prefer packing hits if they don't prolong tail latency.
oliver: kernel selection side — when a batch mixes cached prefixes (shorter causal path) and cold requests, runtime swaps kernels and rebinds KV buffers, which costs ~0.6ms per swap at scale. multiplies badly for small batches.
ci-bot: benchmark-run #3489 completed: baseline(earlier) 95p=118ms, after-change 95p=208ms, p50 ~ unchanged, throughput -3%. full perf log: https://ci.internal/runs/3489/logs
kevin: thanks CI. suggests it's tail-specific. idea: add a packing heuristic that biases filling batches with prefix-hits first up to X tokens, then close the batch. call it hit-aware-smoothing.
sasha: propose algorithm quickly:
```
# pseudo
for window in queue:
  score = is_cache_hit ? hit_bonus : 0
  accept_until = ewma_token_target + score
  pack requests until token_sum >= accept_until
  flush
```
maria: +1. also we should adjust kernel-selection hooks: avoid rebind if all requests share same cache-state bitmask. if mixed, maybe split into two micro-batches instead of one mixed batch.
kevin: good point. micro-split vs single-mix tradeoff — micro-split adds scheduling overhead, single-mix adds kernel switch. need cost model. we can estimate cost_model = swap_cost * num_swaps + schedule_overhead * num_splits - rpc_savings_from_bigger_batch.
jin: i'll run A/B with 3 configs tomorrow: (A) baseline, (B) hit-aware-smoothing (hit_bonus=32 tokens, ewma_target=64), (C) micro-split-on-mix + conservative packing. will collect p50/p95/p99, kernels-swapped, memcpy bytes.
oliver: include per-batch "kernel_switches" metric and "kv_rebind_bytes" in traces. we want correlation between kernel_switches and p95.
sasha: small note: quantized kernels have different swap cost vs fp16; annotate by model_variant in the traces.
kevin: on rollout plan: start with a canary on dev pool with synthetic workload that emulates high prefix-hit skew and short completions. if stable, roll to prod canary 5% traffic.
maria: 👍 also add a safety fallback: if p95 rises > 20% during canary, auto-revert.
ci-bot: experiment job scheduled: perf-a-b-test-185500 with 3 arms; results will be here: https://ci.internal/experiments/185500
jin: collecting baseline traces now, will attach a summary when done. expected run ~2h.
kevin: if we find hit-aware smoothing reduces kernel switches and keeps p95 within 5% of baseline while improving throughput, this could be default for high-hit workloads.
maria: thanks team — please drop logs and short notes in this thread. i'll add a tiny spec to the runbook with parameters to tweak. :memo:
kevin: one more: consider adding a per-key prefix affinity tag so repeated callers get collocated packing; might reduce repartitioning churn across queues. low priority though.
sasha: noted. will prototype the affinity tag in the batcher shim next week.
maria: ok closing for now, keep updates here. :eyes:
